The actual byte device is the one the finding identifies: the exalted root, וְנִשְׂגָּֽב closing oshb:Prov.18.10 (word 8 of 8) against נִ֝שְׂגָּבָ֗ה at word 6 of oshb:Prov.18.11, contiguous skeleton שגב in 3 verses book-wide (Prov.18.10, 18.11, 29.25 - the last as יְשֻׂגָּֽב) with Prov.18.10|Prov.18.11 the sole adjacent pair, rendered “and are safe” (web:Prov.18.10) and “an unscalable wall” (web:Prov.18.11), verbatim against the staged WEB; together with בְּמַשְׂכִּיתֽוֹ it carries the true-refuge against imagined-refuge antithesis. The proposed field repair is byte-supported and endorsed as a proposal only, with one qualification: making the exalted-root recurrence the primary warrant and the strength root a disclosed secondary echo is right, the 10:15 disclosure and the mirrored oshb:Prov.10.15 reference follow the corpus's refs-mirror rule, and the rewritten rival must reject independence on the adjacent-recurrence ground rather than on any built-to-invert claim, which the bytes cannot support.

The bytes corroborate the finding independently of the rendering: 23:24's verb is the long imperfect form of its root, whereas Proverbs itself attests the shortened form of the same root where a wish or prohibition is meant, אַל יָגֵ֥ל at Prov.24.17 words 7-8 and וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל at Prov.23.25 word 4, and accent-stripped substring sweeps keep them apart (the accent-stripped form of 23:24's verb hits 2 of 915, Prov.2.14 in a plural and Prov.23.24; the accent-stripped form of 24:17's short verb hits 1 of 915; the accent-stripped form of 23:25's short verb hits 1 of 915), while the infinitive-absolute-plus-imperfect construction of 23:24 is the assertive intensifier, not a wish.
